The two cars are a single rope-worked pair. One
cannot move without the other moving the same distance
in the opposite direction.

* 0-30 sec.  They are berthed at opposite ends.
The car on the right hand track, big in the right
foreground, is berthed at the cliff top upper station.
The car on the left hand track is berthed in the arch
of the lower station at the foot of the cliff, in
front of the pier building.

* They start together, and keep together.  The
right hand car draws away downhill, getting smaller,
the left hand car comes out of the lower arch uphill,
getting bigger.

* At about the middle of the run, $\approx$ 60-65 sec,
they draw exactly level, side by side in the middle
of the incline, on the parallel tracks.

* The down car goes on downhill, shrinking, and is
last seen dropping in behind the up car toward the
lower station arch.  The up car goes on uphill,
growing, until in the last frames, 80-86 sec, its
red and cream end, with the black roof, fills the
centre foreground at the head of the incline, entering
the upper landing the down car left.

They started opposite, passed in the exact middle,
and move at the identical cable speed.  They
necessarily berth at the same moment at opposite ends.

So when the down car comes to rest inside the
lower, tunnel, station at the foot of the cliff, the
up car will come to rest at that same moment inside
the upper station at the top of the cliff, on the
left hand parallel track - in effect the two cars
have simply exchanged the positions they occupied
at the start of the clip.
